I've been working this land for 30 years. My father farmed before me. I know what works here in Quzhou — the soils, the wells, when the rains come and when they don't. I don't take risks I don't need to.

**My thinking:**

My 50 mu rotates fully — wheat goes in after maize harvest in October, maize goes in after wheat harvest in June. Same land, both seasons. That's how it's always been done here and it works.

For wheat, I'll use Jimai 22 — I've planted it for years, the local seed station carries it, I know how it performs on my fields. I put base fertilizer down before seeding and topdress at jointing. I irrigate four times: before sowing to get good germination, then overwintering water to protect the roots, then jointing, then heading. That's standard. I spray once for weeds early and once for rust and powdery mildew in spring. My rotary tiller goes over the field after maize harvest to break up the stubble.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the county seed shop has that's similar and reliable. I direct-seed into the wheat stubble, no tillage needed, saves me labor and my sons aren't always home to help. I apply more nitrogen to maize, it needs it in the heat. I irrigate at germination if it's dry, definitely at tasseling, and at grain filling. I watch for corn borer and spray if I see it.

My family needs the grain income. Some of my kids work in the city but the farm is still the foundation. I won't experiment with anything strange this year.
